Use case: stylized-concept. Make ONE production-ready transparent sprite atlas for a cozy pet discovery game: EXACTLY six equal columns and four equal rows, 24 separate tiles. No labels, text, visible grid, checkerboard or background. Read row-major: each consecutive PAIR has (left) a standalone edible item and (right) its MATCHING collectible stamp. Each row contains three pairs. Twelve pairs in this exact order: 1: round pale Korean pear; 2: curved yellow banana; 3: purple grape cluster; 4: two red cherries on stems; 5: three blue blueberries; 6: golden orange mango; 7: green sliced kiwi with brown skin; 8: small golden pineapple with green crown; 9: coconut half with white flesh; 10: purple fig cut open with pink flesh; 11: pink dragon fruit with green tips and white speckled slice; 12: pale green melon half.
The standalone food is a cute recognizable generous-volume miniature, clean warm taupe outline, clear juicy color, restrained cream highlight, gentle matte cel shading, rounded forms, no face or limbs. Slight three-quarter view, whole item fully visible, 65% of tile footprint, no cast ground shadow. Not emoji-font imitation, blurry watercolor, photographic or pixel art. All foods share the same line weight and camera.
The paired stamp contains that SAME food, color and identifying silhouette, inside a small cream embossed round paper seal with a delicate scalloped warm-beige edge and tiny botanical flecks. Food occupies most of the seal; no text, numerals, stars, rarity badges or detached decorative confetti. Give standalone and stamp equal clear tile spacing, each fully inside its own cell with 15% transparent safe gutters. Genuinely transparent alpha around every item and seal. High-resolution crisp game icon rendering for small 40px food and 64px stamps.
